items.titulo: AWS Releases AWS Emulator: A Local Copy of 200+ AWS Services Built by AI Agents
items.resumen: AWS released AWS Emulator, a free, CC0-licensed local emulator of AWS APIs built from 438 API models. Autonomous agents wrote all of its code. It passes 56.6% of 42,857 published fidelity tests at launch. The post AWS Releases AWS Emulator: A Local Copy of 200+ AWS Services Built by AI Agents appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items.titulo: aws-emulator
items.resumen: aws-emulator Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so. It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog. It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great

items.titulo: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen
Gemini Decisions API
items.resumen: Gemini Decisions API Google join Jev and OpenAI in the decision model category with "Gemini Decision 1". This new model API is almost identical to Jev: it supports the same three types of questions (yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring) and even reuses Jev's term "Noul" for a yes/no question. It's priced the same as the GPT-6 Luna decision model: 10 cents per million input tokens, and output is free. Jev remains the cheapest of the three, at 4.2 cents per million.
